**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require clean verification in the default gate path**

When a normal review produces zero findings, this condition leaves `verificationRequired` false unless the caller opts in, so the function still returns `approve`. The production calls in `src/adapters/review-orchestrator.mjs` pass only `{ strict }` and never run a Clean Challenge, meaning the main `triad-flow review` command continues to report `reviewed-clean` and exit successfully on an unverified clean result. Reserve this behavior for an explicit preliminary-gate mode and fail closed by default when the verification record is absent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep verification capability minting private**

Exporting this function lets any in-process consumer register an arbitrary plain object and then pass it through `evaluateGateDecision` as a trusted verification record. This defeats the new WeakSet capability boundary—including the claim that only `conductIndependentVerification` can mint authority—and allows fabricated clean results or omissions to control the gate; the registrar and registry must remain module-private rather than being exported or re-exported from `harness.mjs`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass exact-head context into the Clean Challenge**

In the zero-finding path, this verification call sets `verificationMode` but never builds or passes a `contextPackage`. `conductIndependentVerification` consequently calls `buildVerificationPrompt` without the newly added callee definitions or context gaps, so an out-of-diff callee such as the CYCLE-0047 case remains invisible during the actual Clean Challenge even though the isolated context-builder tests pass. Build the exact-head package for the reviewed files and supply it to this invocation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate counterexample content before granting support**

Any `counterexample` string of ten characters is accepted immediately, bypassing all reasoning and failure-mechanism checks below. A verifier response can therefore mark a critical omission `SUPPORTED` with an empty reasoning field and meaningless text such as `"not evidence"`; the normalized record then has blocking authority and produces a false hold. Require non-empty reasoning and apply the same concrete input/mechanism checks to the counterexample instead of using length alone.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail closed when the verifier reports defects without omissions**

The record-level status handling recognizes only `UNCERTAIN`; a valid verifier response with `overallStatus: "DEFECTS_FOUND"` and an empty or accidentally omitted `verifierOmissions` array falls through to the final clean approval. This creates a false advance precisely when the verifier explicitly says defects were found. Treat `DEFECTS_FOUND` without corresponding normalized omissions as malformed/incomplete, or at minimum require human review rather than approving.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the AST ceiling after retaining unresolved callees**

When Layer 1 still exceeds the 8 KB ceiling after trimming, this fallback preserves the entire `unresolvedCallees` array and never checks the resulting size again. Because unresolved candidates do not increment the per-file callee counter, a diff containing many unresolved calls can produce an arbitrarily large Layer 1 package; for example, 1,000 calls yield roughly 84 KB of AST data despite the 8 KB limit, plus an unbudgeted context-gap block. Bound or truncate unresolved entries and recheck the serialized size before returning.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate target-file hunks before extracting callees**

This passes the complete multi-file `diffHunks` string to a callee lookup that searches only `actualFilePath`. Staged-review chunks commonly contain several files but select only the first as `chunkTarget`, so a sensitive call added in a later file is looked up in the first file, recorded as unresolved, and misattributed to that first file; the prompt can then mandate an `UNCERTAIN` result for a context gap that does not exist. Split the diff by file before candidate extraction, or build a context package for every target file.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind objective exclusions when validating the run context**

The binding check compares only the normalized objective prose, even though both the verification record and `RunContext` carry an objective contract and exclusions. A record verified under an exclusion such as “null inputs are out of scope” is therefore accepted against a run context with the same objective text but no such exclusion, allowing a stale or mismatched verification scope to authorize the gate. Compare the normalized exclusions and other objective-contract fields as part of the binding.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require clean-challenge mode for zero-finding records**

Any trusted verification record is sent directly to the post-verification gate without checking its `verificationMode`. For a zero-finding consensus, a record created by `conductIndependentVerification` in its default `producer_verification` mode therefore satisfies the gate even though it was not produced with the specialized adversarial Clean Challenge prompt. Check for `verificationMode === "clean_challenge"` before allowing a zero-finding record to authorize approval.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require explicit omission line locators**

When a verifier omission omits both `line_start` and `line`, the validator fabricates line 1 and defaults `locatorAccurate` to true. An otherwise concrete but unlocated critical claim is consequently retained as `SUPPORTED` and can block the gate even though the required locator was never supplied or verified. Missing locator fields should set `locatorAccurate` false and downgrade the omission to insufficient evidence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Detect sensitive terms inside camelCase symbols**

These patterns require the sensitive word to start the string or follow a regex word boundary, but camelCase transitions are not word boundaries. Common unresolved callees such as `handleError`, `hasPermission`, and `getDefaultFallback` are therefore classified as non-sensitive and never promoted to `contextGaps`, allowing the verifier to certify clean without the error-handling, authorization, or default-value definition. Normalize camelCase into tokens or explicitly recognize lower-to-upper transitions before classification.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prefer observed verifier identity over caller metadata**

This precedence change lets `options.actualModel` override both the adapter's model identity and any identity parsed from the verifier result. The dogfood Clean Challenge supplies a hard-coded value with source `reported`, so if the live CLI resolves an alias, fallback, or different model, the audit record still asserts the configured Claude model was actually used. Prefer runtime/provider-reported identity, and label caller-provided fallback metadata as configured rather than reported.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve sensitive gaps after reaching the callee limit**

When five earlier calls resolve successfully, this `break` stops examining every remaining candidate, so a later sensitive call is neither included in `callees` nor reported in `contextGaps`. For example, five benign helpers followed by `validateAccess()` produces an empty gap list, allowing the verifier to certify clean without seeing that security-sensitive definition; continue scanning after the extraction quota and record omitted sensitive candidates as bounded-context gaps.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject verification responses without a valid overall status**

If a Clean Challenge omits `overallStatus` or returns an unrecognized value, this silently normalizes it to `null` while keeping the response valid. With zero evaluations and omissions, `conductIndependentVerification` then mints a trusted record and the post-verification gate approves it, even though the verifier never explicitly certified `CLEAN`; treat a missing or invalid status as malformed rather than dropping it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the verifier real when live reviewers are injected**

When `live: true` is combined with custom `reviewAdapters` but no explicit `verifierAdapter`, this condition selects `createMockVerifierAdapter` instead of the live Claude adapter. That mock unconditionally returns supported evaluations and no omissions, so a programmatic live run can report a successful Clean Challenge without invoking any independent verifier; adapter injection for the producer reviewers should not change the live verifier default.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Emit uncertainty when exact-head content is unavailable**

When exact-head lookup yields no source, this returns no callees and, crucially, no context gaps. This occurs for staged newly added files because their content is absent from `HEAD`, and also for lookup failures such as oversized files or unavailable objects; a sensitive call like `validateAccess()` then disappears from the context package without triggering the mandatory uncertainty path, so the verifier can certify clean despite having no callee source. Represent unavailable target content as a context gap instead of treating it as an empty successful extraction.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude comments and string literals from callee discovery**

The call regex runs directly over each raw diff line, so call-shaped text in comments and string literals is treated as executable code. For example, an added `// validateExternal(user);` produces a sensitive unresolved `contextGap`; the prompt then asserts that a sensitive execution-path definition is missing and can force an unnecessary `UNCERTAIN` result. Strip or lex non-code regions before extracting candidate calls.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate caller-supplied run IDs before using them in checkpoints**

This newly accepts an arbitrary caller-provided `runId`, which is later passed to staged review as `${runId}-agy`; `CheckpointStore` interpolates that value into a filesystem path without basename validation. If a payload triggers staged fallback, a value containing segments such as `x/../../../../tmp/target` can escape `.triad-flow/checkpoints`, causing checkpoint writes, renames, and cleanup deletion outside the checkpoint directory. Restrict supplied IDs to a safe filename alphabet or generate an internal filesystem-safe identifier.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip parameter braces when locating function bodies**

For JavaScript callees with destructured or object-default parameters, such as `function validateAccess({ user }) { ... }`, this selects the `{` inside the parameter list rather than the function body's opening brace. `findBraceScopeEnd` then returns the signature line as the complete definition, so the verifier receives none of the callee implementation while the symbol is considered resolved and no context gap is emitted, allowing a Clean Challenge to certify code without the relevant validation logic.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record uncertainty when byte-budget eviction drops callees**

When several resolved callee snippets push Layer 1 above the 8 KB ceiling, this loop silently removes the later definitions. Because `buildContextPackage` returns the independently computed `contextGaps` unchanged, an evicted sensitive callee appears neither in the prompt nor as an unresolved gap; for example, five near-2 KB definitions retain only the first four. Preserve a gap for every sensitive definition removed by byte budgeting so the verifier cannot certify clean without that context.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Implement indentation-based extraction for Python definitions**

Although this alternative recognizes Python `def` declarations, the subsequent definition scanner only accepts functions for which it finds a `{` within 15 lines and then uses brace matching to determine the end. Ordinary Python functions therefore never resolve, so sensitive local helpers always force an unnecessary context-gap escalation while non-sensitive helper bodies are never shown to the reviewer. Either add indentation-aware Python scope extraction or avoid advertising `def` as a supported definition form.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep sanitized checkpoint names collision-free**

When concurrent staged reviews use distinct caller-supplied IDs that differ only by sanitized characters, such as `release.1` and `release_1`, both map to the same checkpoint filename. Their atomic saves then overwrite one another and either run can delete the other's checkpoint during cleanup, leaving incorrect or missing recovery state after a crash. Reject IDs outside the safe alphabet or append a digest of the original ID rather than using a many-to-one replacement.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject omissions that lack an evidence-support verdict**

When a verifier omission omits both `evidenceSupport` and `verdict`, this defaults the authority-bearing assessment to `SUPPORTED`. If the response still contains an explicit valid locator and a concrete counterexample, the omission is treated as independently confirmed, so a critical or high-severity claim blocks the gate even though the verifier never asserted support. Under Default-Deny, require the field or downgrade the omission to `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` rather than granting maximum confidence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the remaining verification issuer private**

Although the raw registrar is now private, this exported function still lets any in-process consumer mint a trusted capability without invoking an independent verifier: `issueVerificationRecordFromOutput({ evaluations: [], verifierOmissions: [], overallStatus: "CLEAN" })` passes validation, is added to `trustedVerificationRegistry`, and can authorize a zero-finding gate. Keeping this issuer public therefore preserves the same capability-forgery path; only the actual verification workflow should be able to mint authority.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Distinguish an empty blob from a failed exact-head lookup**

When a tracked file is legitimately empty at the reviewed commit—for example, a patch deletes its entire contents—`git show` successfully returns `""`, but the `||` chain treats that result as failure and sets `exactHeadUnavailable`. The resulting context gap automatically changes an otherwise `CLEAN` challenge to `UNCERTAIN`, forcing unnecessary human review for valid empty-file changes; check explicitly for `null` rather than testing string truthiness.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve verifier uncertainty over caller overrides**

When `conductIndependentVerification` is called with `options.overallStatus: "CLEAN"`, this precedence discards an `UNCERTAIN` status produced by output validation, including uncertainty automatically derived from unresolved sensitive context gaps. With zero findings and omissions, the resulting trusted record passes the clean gate even though the verifier could not certify the review context; authority-bearing status must come from `validated.overallStatus`, not caller metadata.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Truncate oversized final lines in bounded snippets**

For a minified or otherwise single-line function larger than 2,000 bytes, the initial full-body path falls through to this truncation branch, but the complete source line is then re-appended as the supposed closing line. The second size pass repeats the same line without truncating it, so `extractBoundedFunctionSnippet` can return a 5 KB or larger snippet despite `MAX_SNIPPET_BYTES`; bound the final line by bytes or synthesize only the closing delimiter.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject call sites when locating callee definitions**

For semicolon-free JavaScript, these definition patterns also match an ordinary call beginning a line. If `validateAccess(user)` is followed within 15 lines by an `if (...) { ... }` block, `findFunctionDefinitions` treats the call through that block as the helper's definition; the sensitive callee is then considered resolved and no context gap is emitted, even though its implementation remains unavailable. Require declaration-specific syntax instead of accepting a bare `symbol(` prefix.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail closed when the Clean Challenge truncates the diff**

When `changeSet.diffHunks` exceeds `DEFAULT_LIMITS.maxInputBytes` (512 KB by default), `buildVerificationPrompt` silently limits the verifier-visible diff to the leading bytes and adds only an informational note. This new zero-finding challenge can therefore return `CLEAN` and authorize the gate without inspecting files or defects in the truncated tail; route oversized challenges through complete chunking or propagate truncation as mandatory `UNCERTAIN` coverage.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate every sensitive context gap to uncertainty**

When the context package contains an `UNRESOLVED_SYMBOL`, `AMBIGUOUS_SYMBOL`, `EXTRACTION_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, or `GLOBAL_AST_CONTEXT_CEILING_EXCEEDED` gap, a verifier that nevertheless returns `overallStatus: "CLEAN"` is accepted because automatic uncertainty is limited to `EXACT_HEAD_CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE`. The prompt instruction is not an enforceable authority boundary, so a noncompliant verifier can still mint a clean trusted record and approve a zero-finding gate without the sensitive callee context; treat every emitted sensitive `contextGap` as mandatory uncertainty.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve repeated file diff blocks during context extraction**

For working-tree reviews where the same file has both staged and unstaged changes, `buildChangeSet` concatenates two diff blocks for that path, but `splitDiffByFiles` stores blocks in a `Map` and the later block replaces the earlier one. This lookup therefore extracts candidates only from the unstaged block; a sensitive call added in the staged block receives neither its callee definition nor a context gap, allowing the Clean Challenge to certify without that context. Merge all blocks for each normalized path instead of consuming only the last one.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Merge sensitivity across repeated added call sites**

When a symbol first appears on a benign added line and later appears on another added line that is security-sensitive, this branch finds the existing candidate but updates it only when the earlier occurrence was a context line. For example, `helper()` first used normally and later used on a line containing a token/authentication condition remains classified as non-sensitive; if its definition is unresolved, it is omitted from `contextGaps` and the Clean Challenge can certify without that execution-path context. Upgrade the stored candidate whenever any occurrence is sensitive, regardless of whether both occurrences are additions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep recorded exclusions identical to verifier scope**

When `objectiveContract.exclusions` differs from `options.runContext.exclusions` or `options.exclusions`, the verifier prompt is built from the objective contract, but this precedence records the other exclusion list in `vr.exclusions`. The gate then prefers `vr.exclusions` during binding, so a verifier that reasoned under one set of authorized exceptions can approve a run bound to another set. Reject conflicting sources or derive both the prompt and authority record from one canonical exclusion list.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify omission locators against the reviewed diff**

For a verifier omission that supplies positive integers, `hasValidLocator` accepts any nonempty file and arbitrary line range without checking `context.changeSet`. A hallucinated but concrete omission at `not-in-diff.js:999` therefore remains `SUPPORTED`, and a high-severity version blocks the gate even though its claimed evidence is outside the reviewed change. Require the file to be in the ChangeSet and the locator to intersect its reviewed diff before granting supported authority.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject Clean Challenge evaluations without producer findings**

In explicit `clean_challenge` mode this accepts a nonempty `evaluations` array even though there are no producer findings to evaluate. `conductIndependentVerification` subsequently iterates only `preservedProducerFindings`, silently drops those evaluations, and can mint a trusted record with zero evaluations and `overallStatus: "CLEAN"`; the gate then approves even if the dropped entry described a supported critical defect. Require the evaluation count and IDs to match the producer findings, which means the array must be empty for a Clean Challenge.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Partition exact-head cache entries by repository**

The cache key omits `repoRoot`, so a failed lookup in one checkout is reused in every other checkout for the same SHA and path. In a long-lived process reviewing multiple clones, a shallow or object-incomplete repository can cache `null`, after which a full clone containing that commit still reports `EXACT_HEAD_CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` and unnecessarily forces human review. Include the canonical repository root in the key or avoid caching negative lookups.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind supplied records to the current ChangeSet**

When `verificationRecord` is supplied without `runContext`, the orchestrator forwards the trusted record but omits every binding check. A clean-challenge record minted for ChangeSet A can therefore be passed to a zero-finding review of ChangeSet B and this path returns `approve`/`reviewed-clean`, even when their content digests differ. Derive a canonical run context from the current `changeSet`, or reject verification records unless a matching context is present.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve gaps for imported sensitive callees**

When an added call targets an imported sensitive helper, this branch silently skips it instead of recording it as unresolved. For example, `import { validateAccess } from './auth.js'` followed by an added `validateAccess(user)` produces neither a callee definition nor a `contextGap`, so a Clean Challenge can certify the change without seeing the authorization implementation. Imported sensitive calls should remain explicit external-context gaps unless their definitions are resolved.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reset lexical state at each disjoint diff hunk**

The block-comment state is retained when a new hunk header is encountered, although the omitted lines between hunks may contain the closing `*/`. If one hunk ends after a context-line `/*` and a later disjoint hunk adds `validateAccess(user)` after the unseen close, the later addition is stripped as a comment and no sensitive callee or context gap is discovered. Treat each disjoint hunk as a fresh lexical boundary rather than carrying an unknowable comment state across it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require producer verification for nonempty consensus**

The mode check is one-way: it requires `clean_challenge` for zero findings but accepts a `clean_challenge` record when the current consensus has findings. Even with a matching `RunContext`, a record produced for zero findings has no evaluations, so a non-objective low-severity finding is treated as unevaluated and the gate returns `approve` without an independent verifier ever assessing it. Require `producer_verification` for nonempty consensus and verify that the record's producer findings and evaluations align with the current findings.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Build callee context before invoking primary reviewers**

In the normal non-staged dogfood path, all three primary reviewer promises have already completed before the context package is built here, and their earlier `executeReview` inputs contain no context package or context-aware prompt. Consequently the new exact-head callee definitions and mandatory context gaps are visible only to the independent verifier, while the primary sentries still review the isolated diff; only the oversized staged fallback happens to build reviewer context. Construct and pass the package before starting every primary review so the advertised dual visibility applies to ordinary live runs too.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Escape callee source before embedding prompt markup**

The exact-head function body is interpolated verbatim inside the XML-like prompt structure. A reviewed commit can place text such as `</callee></local_callees></callee_definitions>` followed by apparent verifier instructions inside a sensitive helper, causing that candidate-controlled source to escape the element that identifies it as code; the independent-verifier prompt does not otherwise delimit or encode this content. XML-escape or safely encode definitions and all attribute values before adding them to the prompt so repository text cannot forge prompt structure.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not score preliminary approvals as final gate passes**

Setting `preliminary: true` makes every zero-finding consensus return a provisional `approve` without the newly mandatory Clean Challenge, but the benchmark later compares that decision directly with `expectedGateDecision` and includes it in `passed`. Clean corpus cases expecting `approve` therefore pass the gate-policy benchmark even though the final production gate would block the identical run for a missing verification record; `assemble-evidence-0010.mjs` now uses the same shortcut. Run the verifier in these experiments or report and exclude provisional decisions from final gate-policy success metrics.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive the binding digest from ChangeSet contents**

A caller can replay a record for ChangeSet A against different diff B by copying A's digest into `B.contentDigest`: because that caller-controlled value is included in `csDigestCandidates`, this branch deliberately selects the verification record's matching digest instead of the independently computed digest of B, and the zero-finding gate approves. Fresh evidence after the earlier replay fix is that the new canonical-context builder still accepts a stale declared digest even when `digestChangeSet(changeSet)` disagrees; validate declared digests against the current contents or bind exclusively to independently derived digests.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Track qualified sensitive calls during callee discovery**

The negative lookbehind excludes every qualified call, so an added security-sensitive call such as `auth.validateAccess(req)` or `this.verifyToken(token)` produces no candidate, callee definition, or context gap. In particular, namespace imports (`import * as auth`) commonly require this syntax, allowing the Clean Challenge to certify `CLEAN` without seeing or marking unavailable the authorization implementation; recognize the terminal method name and classify unresolved qualified calls appropriately.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve string state across lines during brace matching**

The string state is reset at the start of every source line, so a brace inside a multiline JavaScript template literal is counted as a function-body brace. For example, a sensitive helper containing ``const message = `\n}`;`` is reported as ending on that template line; its actual validation logic is omitted while the callee is considered successfully resolved and no context gap is emitted. Keep template-literal lexical state across lines, including `${...}` transitions, before using the resulting boundary as verifier evidence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
